label: Blocking cost of preventing suffering: An outcome counterfactually unavoidable in preventing this…
definition: An outcome counterfactually unavoidable in preventing this suffering: loss of an unreplaceable greater good or permission of an evil at least as bad. The greater-good relation allows justice and no temporal restriction. An actually connected good, without necessity, is insufficient. This is Rowe’s simplified necessary-condition vocabulary; it does not make the cost morally sufficient, and it does not formalize the balance-neutral-good refinement in p.336 n.3.
